blocks.title: Permutations and combinations
blocks.md: A **permutation** counts ordered arrangements, a **combination** counts unordered selections of r items from n (written ⁿPᵣ and ⁿCᵣ):

blocks.title: Useful rules
blocks.md:
- n! = n(n − 1)…1 and 0! = 1.
- n objects with p identical of one kind: n!/p! arrangements.
- ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ and ⁿPᵣ = r! × ⁿCᵣ.
- 'At least one' = total − none.

blocks.title: Order or not?
blocks.md: Ask: does the **order** matter? Seats, ranks, passwords, president/secretary: permutation. Committees, teams, hands of cards: combination. For a restricted position (for example the last digit must be even), fill that position **first**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using a permutation when order does not matter (a committee).
- Forgetting repeated letters: CAMEROON has two Os.
- For 'at least one', adding many cases instead of using total − none.

blocks.title: Example 1: arrangements
blocks.statement: In how many ways can 5 pupils fill 3 prefect posts (distinct posts)? In how many ways can the letters of CAMEROON be arranged?
steps: CAMEROON has 8 letters with the letter O twice: 8! ÷ 2! = 40 320 ÷ 2.

blocks.title: Example 2: selections
blocks.statement: A committee of 3 is chosen from 5 men and 4 women. How many committees (a) in all (b) with at least one woman? How many even 4-digit numbers can be made from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 without repeats?
steps: (a) ⁹C₃ = 84. (b) No women: ⁵C₃ = 10, so at least one woman: 84 − 10 = 74.

lessons.title: Probability: addition, conditional and tree diagrams
lessons.programRef: O Level Further Mathematics — Permutations, combinations, probability, statistics (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
Use tree diagrams with and without replacement.
reviewNotes: Conditional probability and tree diagrams: confirm the syllabus.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Rules
blocks.md: Addition rule; independent events; conditional probability:
blocks.tex: P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) \qquad P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B) \ \text{(independent)} \qquad P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}

blocks.title: Tree diagrams
blocks.md: Draw a branch for each outcome and write its probability. **Multiply** along a path (AND) and **add** the paths that give the event (OR). Without replacement the second-stage probabilities change; with replacement they stay the same. 'At least one' = 1 − P(none).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Adding instead of multiplying along a branch.
- Not changing the denominator when items are not replaced.
- Treating events as independent when they are not (mutually exclusive events with P > 0 are **not** independent).

blocks.title: Example 1: without replacement
blocks.statement: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Find P(both red), P(one of each) and P(at least one red).

blocks.title: Example 2: independent events
blocks.statement: P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5 are independent. Find P(A ∩ B), P(A ∪ B), and P(A | B).
steps: P(A | B) = 0.2 ÷ 0.5 = 0.4 = P(A), as expected for independent events.

lessons.title: Variance and standard deviation
lessons.programRef: O Level Further Mathematics — Permutations, combinations, probability, statistics (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Calculate the variance and standard deviation of raw data and of a frequency table.
Describe the effect of adding to or multiplying the data.
Compare two sets of data using mean and standard deviation.
reviewNotes: Variance and standard deviation: the course may use the population formula (divide by n) or the sample formula (n - 1): confirm which one the Cameroon syllabus uses; this lesson divides by n.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Variance and standard deviation
blocks.md: For n values with mean x̄ (and, for a table, frequencies f with Σf = n):

blocks.title: Effect of changing the data
blocks.md: If every value is increased by k, the mean increases by k but the standard deviation is **unchanged**. If every value is multiplied by k, the mean and the standard deviation are both multiplied by k (the variance by k²).

blocks.title: Comparing
blocks.md: The data set with the **smaller standard deviation** is more consistent (less spread). Compare the means first, then the spread: 'similar mean but smaller σ means more consistent'.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Forgetting to square root: the variance is in squared units.
- Subtracting the mean squared from Σx² without dividing by n first: it is Σfx²/Σf − x̄².
- Using σ when the question gives the sample (n − 1) version: check which one the course uses.

blocks.title: Example 1: raw data
blocks.statement: Find the mean, variance and standard deviation of 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.

blocks.title: Example 2: a table
blocks.statement: x = 2, 3, 4, 5 with frequencies 1, 3, 4, 2. Find the mean and standard deviation. If the data are doubled and 5 added, find the new mean and σ.
